The exact W1p extension operator transfers the whole-space p* inequality, with the finite-dimensional Euclidean-gradient/coordinate-norm comparison stated. The p=1 endpoint is supplied by compact smooth density, complete L^(n/(n-1)) convergence and nested a.e. subsequences identifying the class; it is not incorrectly imported as a whole-space W11 theorem. Holder interpolates p<=q<=p*; endpoints are direct and the empty domain has the zero class. AC is explicit, as required by the transfer and smooth-extension suppliers. Constants depend on the fixed extension domain/operator, not uniformly over all domains.

The exact Wkp extension is multiplied by a fixed cutoff, so the proof iterates whole-space inequalities on compact support and does not presume lower-order extension operators on Omega. Order descent uses all actual weak-commutation hypotheses; invariant r-n/q is preserved. At kp<n the last source exponent stays below n and gives np/(n-kp); finite-measure Holder supplies all q>=1 below it. At kp=n the last space is W1n and Holder lowers the source exponent to nq/(n+q) before GNS, giving all finite q. At kp>n iteration reaches q>n or q=n with at least two derivatives remaining; the latter gives arbitrarily large finite q_prime, and the former order-1 case gives exactly the allowed fractional endpoint. Morrey controls all required derivatives on a fixed ambient ball, and the internally explained uniform-mollification segment identity converts continuous weak derivatives to classical derivatives. The closure norm and empty convention are explicit. Added AC from Given and the current embedding/extension suppliers.
